title: Clopen sections compute stalks and detect zero etale sheaves
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $C$ be a commutative $K$-algebra, and put $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that $K\to C_z$ is an isomorphism for every prime $z\subset C$, where $C_z$ denotes localization at the complement of $z$, and that clopen subsets form a basis of the topology of $E$. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $E$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For each geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$ over $z$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the restriction maps induce a canonical isomorphism $$\varinjlim_{W\ni z,\ W\ \mathrm{clopen}}G(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\bar z},$$ where the transition maps are restriction to smaller clopen neighbourhoods and the geometric stalk is that of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The canonical germ map $G(E)\to G_{\bar z}$ is surjective; in particular $G(E)=0$ implies $G_{\bar z}=0$ for every geometric point. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, every abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $T$, and every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, the canonical germ map $F(T)\to F_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism.
